en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: To acquaint students with the problems of food analysis and basic principles of instrumental methods.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Methods used in food analysis (allowance 2/0) a.chemical methodsb.physico-chemical methods2.Chromatographic and electrophoretic, optical distribution and determination principles (allowance 2/0) a.physical and their extentb.optical methods and their principles3.electrochemical methods, classification and measurement principles (allowance 2/0) a.conductometric titrationb.potentiometric titration4.gas chromatography and its applications (allowance 2/0) a.instrumentation componentsb.detectors5.Thermodynamics of separation (allowance 2/0) a.retention volume and retention timeb.chromatographic column efficiency6.factors to distinguish column separation (allowance 2/0) a.efficiency factorb.selectivity factorc.capacity factor7.Analytical information from the chromatogram (allowance 2/0) a.quantitative informationb.external standardc.standard addition method8.Solid phase microextraction (allowance 2/0) a.the principle of attachment to the fiberb.determination of adsorption time9.Mass spectrometry (allowance 2/0) a.essence of mass spectrometryb.spectra of positively charged ions10.Application of mass spectrometry (allowance 2/0) a.organic pollutants from the environmentb.GC-MS for analysis of esters and other fragrance compounds11.Principle and application of HPLC (allowance 2/0) a.instrumentation componentsb.detectors and design principles12.HPLC application (allowance 2/0) a.Use in food industryb.mass range on columns for food analysis
